question.problem: The axis of symmetry of $y=(x-2k)(x+3k)$ is $x=-2.$ The value of $k=$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2,$ we will set our result equal to $-2.$ 

From the equation $y=(x-2k)(x+3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=2k$ and ${x}_{2}=-3k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2k+(-3k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-k}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-2.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-k}{2} & =-2 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
